notes:
Controller: model-based pick-and-place state machine using the private MuJoCo model for IK (damped least squares on the grasp site, 6-DoF pose).

Phases: plan -> pre (joint-space move to an IK pose 12 cm above the cube) -> descend (Cartesian, tracks the cube's observed xy, grasp site placed at cube centre height, 1 cm toward the thumb so the cube sits deep in the fingers) -> grasp (closure ramp 0.6 s, hold) -> lift (Cartesian to z=table+0.21, verifies cube came along; otherwise re-plans, up to the time limit) -> carry (joint-space move to a precomputed IK pose above the destination bin) -> lower (joint-space to a pose 9.5 cm above the table at the bin centre, with misalignment retry) -> release (open 0.4 s) -> retract (and re-plan if the cube is not in the bin).

Planning: candidate hand yaws are the cube yaw + k*90deg (and 45deg diagonals as fallback); each is checked by IK from home for both grasp and pre-grasp poses plus a self-collision / table-collision check (thumb grazing the table allowed), with a cost combining distance to a position-dependent preferred yaw (keeps the wrist away from the torso for cubes near the body midline) and a penalty if another cube lies in the finger footprint. The carry yaw is chosen similarly to be feasible for the bin at both carry and place heights (left bin ~ +0.3 rad, right bin ~ -0.4 rad).

Tested: 100+ practice seeds nominal with 100% success after fixes; also run in-sandbox under the noisy_sensing, heavy_slippery and weak_motors variants (30 seeds each) with all successes.

Known weaknesses: if the target cube ends up far outside the normal layout (e.g. pushed to x>0.3) grasps become less reliable; a cube knocked into the wrong bin is not recovered; no explicit avoidance of neighbouring cubes beyond the yaw penalty; self-collision check uses zero clearance margin.
